Hanabiko "Koko" (born July 4, 1971 at the San Francisco Zoo) is a female western lowland gorilla who is known for having learned a large number of hand signs from a modified version of American Sign Language (ASL). She is reportedly able to understand more than 1,000 signs of what her trainer calls "Gorilla Sign Language" (GSL).

Koko is one of the few non-humans known to keep a pet. Researchers at The Gorilla Foundation said that Koko asked for a cat for Christmas in 1983. When she was given a lifelike stuffed animal, she was less than satisfied. She did not play with it and continued to sign "sad." So on her birthday in July 1984, she was able to choose a kitten from a litter. Koko selected a gray male Manx from a litter of abandoned kittens and named him "All Ball". In December of that same year, All Ball escaped from Koko's cage and was hit and killed by a car. Her trainer said that when she signed to Koko that All Ball had been killed, Koko signed "Bad, sad, bad" and "Frown, cry, frown, sad". Here is a video of her with All Ball and then reacting to news of his death.

In 1985, Koko was allowed to pick out two new kittens from a litter to be her companions. The animals she chose, she named "Lipstick" and "Smokey," were also Manxes. More recently, to celebrate her birthday in October 2015, Koko was presented another litter of kittens. Picking two, she named them Miss Black and Miss Grey.
